diagnostic_evidence.quote: The proposed method is not only asymptotic-preserving as $\eps \to 0$ but also uniformly accurate for $0<\eps\le 1$,
leading to a uniform accuracy of $ O\big( \tau^{2/7} + h^{2/5} \big) $ in the maximum norm for all $ 0 < \eps \leq 1 $.

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract and introduction claim uniform accuracy/convergence for 0<eps<=1 and second-order accuracy with tau,h unrestricted by eps. The only proved bounds are O(tau^2+h^2+eps) (O(eps^2) for polarized data). These do not tend to zero as tau,h->0 for fixed eps, and are O(1) for eps~1. The paper's own Remark gives only O(tau^{2/7}+h^{2/5}) uniformly over 0<eps<=1, and that rate relies on switching to a classical bound with eps^{-6}, eps^{-4} factors. So the claimed uniform second-order accuracy over the whole range 0<eps<=1 is not established; second order holds only up to an O(eps) (resp. O(eps^2)) floor.

failure_location.quote: The methods are uniformly convergent in the range from arbitrarily small to moderately bounded~$\eps$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the claims: second-order in tau,h up to an O(eps) (O(eps^2) polarized) modulation error, accurate for small eps. State the uniform-in-eps guarantee as the Remark's O(tau^{2/7}+h^{2/5}) combined bound, or drop 'uniformly accurate/convergent'.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised scope (uniformly accurate and uniformly convergent for 0<eps<=1, second order independent of eps) is overstated. The theorems give asymptotic-regime accuracy for small eps. For moderate eps the weighted-scheme bound is not small and the Remark's weaker rate is the only uniform statement.
issues.title: Claims of uniform accuracy and second-order convergence for all eps are not what the theorems give
issues.why_classification: No proof is wrong, but a headline guarantee must be withdrawn and replaced by a weaker, comparable one. This is more than rewording and does not need new proof architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: The reconstructed velocity eps^2 v contains eps^2*(e^{-i alpha}p^{n+1}-e^{i alpha}p^{n-1})/(2 tau) and eps*c_g*(spatial difference)/(2h). Inserting p = a e^{...} + R, the remainder R contributes terms of size (eps^2/tau)||R||_inf and (eps/h)||R||_inf. Theorem th:MFE only bounds ||R||_inf by C(tau^2+h^2+eps), with no bound on the time or space differences of R. For tau << eps^2 or h << eps the amplification factors eps^2/tau and eps/h are unbounded. The claimed uniform velocity bound O(tau^2+h^2+eps), with constants independent of eps,tau,h, therefore does not follow. The stability lemma controls only (e^{n+1},e^n), not their differences scaled by eps^2/tau.

failure_location.quote: which, together with Theorem~\ref{th:MFE}, leads to the velocity error estimate in Theorem~\ref{thm}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove a bound on the error of the discrete time and space difference quotients, for example via the transformed-norm stability estimate on e^{n+1}-e^{n-1} and its spatial differences, or restrict the velocity bounds to tau >~ eps^2 and h >~ eps with an explicit extra argument.
issues.overall_effect: The velocity estimates in thm and in thm:polarized are unsupported outside the regime tau >~ eps^2 and h >~ eps. The solution error bounds are unaffected.
issues.title: Velocity error bound deduced from a max-norm remainder bound without controlling difference-quotient amplification
issues.why_classification: A contained additional estimate or a limited regime restriction for the velocity part fixes it. The position error bounds and the overall method survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The maximum norm in the defect bound of Lemma~\ref{lem:defect-max} turns out to be too weak a norm for the proof of Theorems~\ref{th:MFE} and~\ref{thm}.

issues.failure_explanation: The nonlinear stability lemma requires the defect in the C([0,T],A(R)) norm. For the general case the paper proves this separately (Lemma lem:defect-wiener) because the max-norm bound is 'too weak'. For polarized data, the Remark states the O(tau^2+h^2+eps^2) defect bound only in L^infty and without proof. The A-norm (or BC^1) version is never established. It needs extra regularity of the corrector b, whose equation has the source partial_t partial_xi a. Theorem thm:polarized is therefore not proved as written.

failure_location.quote: The higher-order accuracy in $\eps$ for the solution $u$ follows from the polarized approximation in Proposition~\ref{prop2} together with the refined defect estimate for the numerical solution given in Remark~\ref{defect-pola}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State and prove the polarized defect bound in the BC^1/Wiener norm, using regularity of a and b, exactly as in the general-data lemma, and cite it in the proof.
issues.overall_effect: The improved O(tau^2+h^2+eps^2) rate for polarized data lacks a valid supporting estimate in the norm required by the stability argument.
issues.title: Polarized error bound relies on a max-norm defect estimate that the paper itself calls insufficient
issues.why_classification: The same Taylor/Wiener-algebra argument as Lemma lem:defect-wiener applies with extra derivatives of a and b. This is a routine local repair that keeps the result and its rate.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: equivalent to the norm $\|\cdot\|_{A(\mathbb{R}) \times A(\mathbb{R})}$ uniformly in $\eps,\tau,h$ subject to \eqref{eq:stability}
Following the same procedure as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:stability} yields the desired result.

issues.failure_explanation: At theta*h=beta one has cos(beta-theta h)=1, so tilde-gamma=1 exactly, and gamma=alpha*omega^2. Then tilde-gamma^2/(1+gamma^2)=1/(1+alpha^2 omega^4), which tends to 1 as alpha=-tau/(omega eps^2)->0. This is allowed by condition (stability), so no uniform mu<1 exists. The eigenvalues of V*V, 2(1 -/+ sqrt(ratio)), then degenerate, V^{-1} is unbounded, and the claimed uniform equivalence with constants 1/2 and 1/sqrt(2(1-mu)) fails. At the CFL boundary one can also have |tilde-gamma|=1 with gamma=0, so the strict inequality |tilde-gamma|<max{1,|gamma|} is false. For Crank-Nicolson, the corresponding quantity |gamma_theta|^2 = 1 + omega^2 tau^2/eps^4 at theta*h=beta tends to 1 as tau/eps^2->0, so the same loss occurs and 'uniformly in eps,tau,h' is not shown.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Impose a strict CFL margin and a lower bound on |alpha| (or let the constants depend on them). Treat tau<<eps^2 via the classical-scheme bound of the Remark, or use a different energy-type stability norm that stays uniformly equivalent as alpha->0.
issues.overall_effect: The stability constants, and hence the constants C in the nonlinear stability lemma and in Theorems th:MFE, thm and thm:polarized, are not uniform in eps,tau,h. They blow up as tau/eps^2->0, or at the CFL limit, contrary to the stated 'independent of eps, tau, h'. For both the explicit and the Crank-Nicolson variants this affects the regime tau << eps^2, which the paper treats separately but still covers in the theorem statements.
issues.title: Uniform norm-equivalence in the linear stability lemmas fails; mu<1 is not guaranteed by the CFL condition
issues.why_classification: The fix is a contained modification: restrict or parametrize the regime, or change the Lyapunov norm. The main regime tau >~ eps^2 and the structure of the proof survive, so there is no major loss.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: but depends on $T$ and on upper bounds of the above term in big brackets and of the $C([0,T],A(\mathbb{R}))$ norm of $p$.

issues.failure_explanation: The Lipschitz bound for |p|^2 p - |tilde-p|^2 tilde-p in the Wiener algebra, from the algebra property, depends on ||p^n||_A of the numerical solution. The recursion vvvert E^n vvvert <= (1+c tau) vvvert E^{n-1} vvvert + ... uses a constant c independent of n. That requires an a priori bound on ||p^n||_A, which is not available for the explicit nonlinear scheme. The proof gives no induction or bootstrap showing that ||e^n||_A stays bounded while the bound is propagated. The statement itself makes C depend on the norm of p, so the result is circular as written.

failure_location.quote: using Lemma~\ref{th:stability} and \eqref{eq:alg} for dealing with the nonlinearity, we obtain

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the standard induction: assume ||e^k||_A <= 1 for k<=n. This bounds ||p^k||_A by ||tilde-p||_A+1 and fixes the Lipschitz constant c. Then show the resulting estimate is below 1 provided tau^2+h^2+eps is small enough, and handle the large-parameter case separately.
issues.overall_effect: The nonlinear stability estimate, and the error theorems built on it, are not established without a missing induction argument. In particular, the C(tau^2+h^2+eps) bound is only meaningful if the right-hand side is small enough to close the bootstrap.
issues.title: Nonlinear stability argument uses a Lipschitz constant depending on the numerical solution without a bootstrap
issues.why_classification: This is a standard local bootstrap that closes the existing Gronwall argument. It needs at most a smallness condition on tau^2+h^2+eps and no new architecture or loss of rate.
